home.title: Welcome to ToolForge
home.subtitle: A fast, secure and lightweight toolbox. All data is processed locally.
home.noPluginsHint: Installed plugins will show up here.

favorites.subtitle: Your favorite tools, one click away.
favorites.emptyHint: Click “Favorite” on a tool page to add it here.

recent.subtitle: Tools you opened recently.
recent.emptyHint: Tools you open will show up here.

history.subtitle: Processing records and long-running tasks.
history.privacy: Stored only in the local SQLite database; sensitive tools such as passwords, keys and encryption are never recorded. Every tool call is recorded separately.
history.emptyHint: Process something in tools such as the formatters, encoders or regex tester and it shows up here.
history.reopen: Open the tool with this input
history.rerun: Run again with the same arguments
history.notRerunnable: Arguments were not saved (sensitive tool or too large), so it cannot run again
history.tasksHint: Runs and logs of long-running tasks; all kept permanently.

settings.storageHint: Preferences, favorites and usage are stored in a local SQLite database.
settings.confirmQuitHint: Ask before closing the window or quitting the app
settings.clipboardSuggestHint: When you open ⌘K, the clipboard text is checked locally and matching tools are listed first
settings.globalShortcutHint: Bring ToolForge to the front and open the command palette from any app
settings.shortcutRecording: Press a new shortcut… (Esc to cancel)
settings.runInBackgroundHint: Closing the window keeps ToolForge in the menu bar / system tray so the shortcut stays available
settings.diagnosticsHint: Save version details, the plugin list, recent task summaries and app logs as a zip to attach to bug reports. Clipboard, task inputs and file contents are never included.
settings.shortcutFailed: The shortcut could not be registered at startup: {{detail}}. Choose another one.

cli.title: Command line
cli.label: tfp commands
cli.hint: Create tfp and tfp-<plugin> commands in ~/.toolforge/bin to run plugins that support the command line from a terminal
cli.installedHint: Commands live in {{dir}} and update when plugins are installed or removed
cli.unavailable: This build does not include the command line tool; build toolforge-cli first during development
cli.path: Add this line to your shell profile (such as ~/.zshrc) so the terminal can find them

agent.title: AI Agent
agent.enabledHint: When on, AI agents connected over MCP (such as Claude Code) can call the functions tools expose. Off by default
agent.connectHint: Add this to your MCP client; it starts tfp mcp to talk to ToolForge without listening on any port
agent.unavailable: This build does not include the tfp command line tool; build toolforge-cli first during development
agent.foldersHint: File paths from agents must be inside these folders; writable folders are readable too
agent.noFolders: No folder is granted yet, so functions that need files are refused
agent.perTool: Turn the command line and AI agent access on or off for each tool from its settings icon under Market → All tools. Everything is on by default.

update.title: Software update
update.latest: You are on the latest version
update.hint: New versions are fetched from GitHub Releases
update.autoHint: Checks in the background on startup; nothing is downloaded automatically

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.emptyHint: Long running work such as hashing files shows live progress and logs here.

quit.title: Quit ToolForge?
quit.description: Are you sure you want to quit? You can also minimize the window and keep it running.
quit.running_one: {{count}} task is still running and will be stopped.
quit.running_other: {{count}} tasks are still running and will be stopped.

about.title: About ToolForge
about.tagline: A fast, secure and lightweight toolbox for developers and power users. Every tool is a plugin, and all data is processed locally in Rust.
about.copyright: © {{year}} devlive-community · Released under the MIT License

links.repositoryHint: Star, fork or contribute on GitHub
links.licenseHint: Free to use, modify and distribute

market.subtitle: Browse all {{count}} tools, read what they do and which permissions they use, and choose which ones appear in the sidebar.

online.hint: Install optional tools from the official plugin index. Plugins run in a WASM sandbox with only the permissions they declare. You can also install a local .tfp package.
online.indexFailed: Could not load the plugin index
online.confirmTitle: Install a plugin without an official signature?
online.confirmHint: The plugin runs in a sandbox but can still process data you give it. Only install plugins from sources you trust.

untrusted.unsigned: The package {{name}} ({{id}}) v{{version}} is unsigned, so its origin and integrity cannot be verified.
untrusted.unknownKey: The package {{name}} ({{id}}) v{{version}} is signed with an unofficial key ({{keyId}}), so its publisher cannot be verified.

online.noAppUpdate: No app update available yet: ToolForge v{{version}}, which this plugin needs, has not been released
online.uptodate: {{name}} is already installed and up to date
online.statsHint: Successful downloads confirmed by clients after integrity checks, counted from the statistics launch.

interfaces.title: Command line & AI Agent
interfaces.manage: Configure command line and AI agent

actions.configure: Configure command line and AI agent access for {{name}}
actions.configureUnsupported: This tool does not support the command line or AI agents yet
actions.notLoaded: The plugin is not loaded, so it cannot be opened

config.title: Configure {{name}}

unsupported.cli: This tool is not available from the command line
unsupported.agent: This tool exposes no functions to AI agents

config.unsupportedHint: You can configure it here once a later version declares an interface

notReady.cli: The tfp commands have not been created; create them in Settings to use the terminal
notReady.agent: AI agent access is off; turn it on in Settings for these settings to apply

enable.cli: Allow the command line to run this tool
enable.agent: Allow AI agents to call this tool

enableHint.cli: When off, no tfp command is created and direct calls are refused
enableHint.agent: When off, AI agents can neither see nor call its functions

config.nativeHint: Built-in tools are not sandboxed, so their functions that use files always ask
config.sensitiveBody: {{name}} handles secrets such as keys and tokens. Once opened, AI agents can pass such data to it and read the results. Open it anyway?
